data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The search for a 44-comparator 13-input network stalls because standard symmetry-breaking constraints in SAT encodings over-prune the search space by forcing the first layer into a canonical matching, which eliminates optimal asymmetric networks.","counterconditions":[{"case":"A formal proof demonstrates that fixing the first layer to a canonical matching preserves optimality for n=13.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A simulation finds a 44-comparator network when the first-layer symmetry breaking is completely relaxed.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The known optimal networks for n<13 all possess a canonical first-layer matching, making the over-pruning hypothesis specific only to n>=13.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Exhaustive search and SAT-based methods often fix the first layer of comparators to a canonical form to break symmetry and shrink the state space. If the true minimal 44-comparator network requires an asymmetric first layer (e.g., containing a cross-channel comparator like (0,12) instead of adjacent pairs), this symmetry-breaking rule prematurely prunes the optimal branch, causing the search to stall at 45 comparators.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
